extracted.intended_audience: Public Information Officers (PIOs), Incident Management Teams, emergency information personnel and trainees
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and operational standards for Public Information Officers (PIOs) and Information Sections on developing Information Operations Plans, staffing and equipping Incident/Joint Information Centers, conducting media/public/dignitary tours, briefing packages, and documenting PIO activities during incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Operations Plan — IC approval and AA notification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Incident Commander (IC) approves this plan. The IC will pass it back to the Agency Administrator (AA), who will want to know the plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An Information Operations Plan ensures everyone is on the same page; it is the blueprint for information management and can range from 2 to 22 pages but is usually short. The IC must approve it and the AA should be informed/review it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Operations Plan — Incident Information Center location and size
rubrics_metrics.description: For a major incident the Information Operations Plan should address Incident Information Center location and size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose IIC location/size based on expected public/media interest and operational needs; location should be findable and near phone resources (see IIC location/capabilities guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Operations Plan — Content requirements for a 72-hour kit
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan should specify content requirements for a kit to operate for up to 72 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare go-kits (travel/day/office bags) in advance with essential supplies and equipment (see Handout 2-3 PIO Go-Kit list).

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Operations Plan — Field information operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Address field information operations if they differ from those of the Information Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define how field-based info activities will be staffed, equipped, and coordinated with the IIC/JIC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Operations Plan — Hours of operation
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan should state hours of operation (after determining the information needs and schedule of the media, agency administrator, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set hours to match media and public needs; some incidents/markets may require 24-hour IIC staffing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Operations Plan — Staffing (day and night operational periods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan should address staffing for day and night operational periods (after identifying who prefers day or night operational periods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify personnel preferences and rotate/assign staff to cover required operational periods; provide detail in resource requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Operations Plan — Communications equipment needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify communications equipment needs (cell and regular phones, fax machines, laptop computers, digital camera, Internet connection, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify exact equipment types and backups; ensure connectivity and test equipment early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Operations Plan — Adequate transportation
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan should identify adequate transportation for the terrain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for vehicles appropriate to terrain/climate and include driver qualification if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Operations Plan — Special community operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Address special community operations (for example, evacuated residents will have a greater need for information, and non-English speaking/special community concerns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include translation/language services, targeted messaging, and outreach plans for vulnerable or special-needs populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PIO oversight of incident tours
rubrics_metrics.description: While it is not necessarily the PIO’s duty to lead the tour, he or she should oversee all aspects of it; tours for key audience members should be well planned and operate under strict protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIO should coordinate tour planning, safety, messaging, and who speaks; decide whether Liaison or PIO will lead and consult IC on allowable information; be willing to refuse tours that compromise safety or incident objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community and public tours — scheduling and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a schedule for tours; assign responsibility; notify affected incident personnel at briefing and share the schedule; notify and include the Agency Administrator as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider posting signs for scheduled tours and keep most PIO staff in camp except for special circumstances (VIP helicopter tours, landowner visits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Media tours — transportation, safety, security, and briefings
rubrics_metrics.description: For media tours (large groups to the incident): plan for transportation (e.g., 4x4s with qualified drivers); prepare for a Safety Briefing given by qualified personnel; notify Security of visiting groups; conduct a verbal Situation Briefing; disseminate a press kit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider having Safety Officer provide the Safety Briefing; identify tour guides, maintain radio contact, communicate locations, and test equipment prior to tours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press kit contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The press kit should include the Incident Action Plan (IAP), maps, definitions, press releases, fact sheets, key messages, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble press kits in advance of tours and distribute during media tours and at the IIC; ensure materials are up-to-date and consistent with messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Briefing packages — importance and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefing packages and staffing of the Information personnel are outlined; briefing packages are important and should be identified in the Information Operations Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefing packages support PIO attendance at Planning Meetings and Operational Period Briefings; include concise, accurate updates, key messages, and materials for staff and media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demobilization Plan — written, communicated, and dynamic
rubrics_metrics.description: The Demobilization Plan must be written, communicated, and available to the Information personnel. The Demobilization Plan is dynamic, so review it and look for updates regularly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep demob information accessible to all Information staff and update as operational timelines change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess information personnel backgrounds and competencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The PIO should be aware of Information personnel’s backgrounds regarding on-the-job training, experience, preferred work hours, core competencies, supervisory backgrounds, media backgrounds, and specialized knowledge and skills (writing, video, radio, computer, graphics, GIS, web, language skills, information gathering).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use assessments to assign tasks, identify training needs, and build appropriate teams (match skills to responsibilities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine staffing needs based on incident factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors that affect public information staffing needs include incident location, size, length, complexity, media involvement and public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate these factors early and order personnel/equipment as soon as possible to meet operational needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place resource requests early and provide full assignment details
rubrics_metrics.description: When ordering personnel and equipment place resource requests as early as possible. Give as much detail about the assignment as possible, such as hotel versus tent accommodations, climate, terrain, whether they need to bring a laptop computer, cell phone, vehicle, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed requests reduce delays and mismatches in equipment/skills; anticipate logistical needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider staff safety when bringing people in
rubrics_metrics.description: When bringing people in, always consider their safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess lodging, travel risks, medical support, and exposure to hazards before assigning staff to an incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and mentoring of Information staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Meet with trainee and Incident Training Officer early in the incident to discuss training needs; provide a good experience by rotating job assignments, diversifying assignments, exposing staff to new challenges; have experienced individuals mentor beginners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate on-the-job training into operational schedules and use experienced staff as formal/informal mentors to build capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: PIO role in Planning Meetings and Operational Period Briefings
rubrics_metrics.description: The PIO is expected to attend Planning Meetings to gather new information and update current information; PIO should list the types of information they may provide in Planning Meetings and Operational Period Briefings. Media attendance at Operational Period Briefings normally must be approved by the Incident Commander.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Planning Meetings to collect authoritative information for messaging; coordinate with IC about media access to briefings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Briefing the Information Staff — stand-up discussions and concision
rubrics_metrics.description: Have stand-up discussions with the Information staff to speed up and be concise. Ask people to explain their day or current things going on, and try to do it in about 1 hour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct short, focused staff briefings to maintain situational awareness and plan daily tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident Information Center (IIC) — core functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The IIC is the official place and source where all requests for incident information are channeled; it is typically located near the phone bank; it is where accurate and timely incident information is compiled, organized, and disseminated to the public and news media; it is the place where social media is monitored and messaging created and disseminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish an IIC when the incident will continue and public/media interest requires an expanded operation; ensure single-point coordination of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: IIC location and capabilities — site requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The IIC should be located where: adequate direct-line telephones are present or can be installed; the ICP can be reached within reasonable time; the media and public can find it; you will not interfere with dispatchers and other incident personnel and they will not interfere with you; there is sufficient floor/ wall space, lighting, and access to tables and chairs; computers, copy machine, fax, and internet connectivity are in place or readily available; there is room to expand the operation if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for preexisting facilities to serve as an IIC and verify equipment availability on arrival.

rubrics_metrics.name: IIC setup — room arrangement, phones, signage and status boards
rubrics_metrics.description: When setting up an IIC, arrange the room to allow foot traffic and maximize wall space; situate tables/chairs so posted information can be easily seen; space telephones far enough apart to avoid interference; locate a phone reserved for internal use only; provide separate space/phone bank for media/public if needed; post a map (preferably with an acetate overlay) and an incident status board; post a sign outside the IIC and a bulletin board outside to reduce foot traffic inside; schedule operating hours to accommodate media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan interior layout for workflow and public/media flow; prepare visual displays (maps/status) that can be quickly updated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplies and equipment for IIC — pre-assembled kits
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplies and equipment for IIC can be ordered during an incident but it is more efficient to have essential supplies assembled ahead of time and stored at the facility or in a transportable kit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain pre-packed supplies and equipment so the IIC can become operational immediately; extract items from agency/unit storages where possible on arrival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Information Center (JIC) — definition and primary customers
rubrics_metrics.description: A JIC is an information facility that is the single point of contact during an ongoing major incident. Its primary customers are the public directly affected by an incident; the general public; all agencies, organizations, individuals, and entities involved in or affected by the incident; elected and appointed officials at every level; and all media (local, regional, national/international).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the JIC to coordinate unified, consistent messaging across organizations participating in incident management.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIC characteristics and coordination requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A JIC may be established at each level of incident management (local, State, regional, national) as required; the JIC includes representatives of each jurisdiction, agency, private-sector entity, and nongovernmental organization involved; responses should accommodate multiple JIC locations when the incident spans wide geographic areas; each JIC must have procedures and protocols to communicate and coordinate effectively with other JICs and other components of Incident Command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish inter-JIC communication/coordination protocols early, and ensure representation from all stakeholders to maintain consistent public information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dignitary visit protocol (Handout 3-1 steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Steps for dignitary visits: determine which elected officials to invite in coordination with AA/IC/local PIO; initiate contact and provide incident information; notify IC and security; confirm departure/return times and areas to be covered; arrange appropriate vehicles; work with Air Operations Branch Director if aircraft needed (note federal restrictions on public aircraft use); assign a tour guide from the PIO Section; provide appropriate safety gear and a Safety Briefing; provide tour guide with list of dignitaries and correct names/titles; determine whether security will accompany and vehicle arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these steps to ensure dignitary visits are safe, controlled, and consistent with incident objectives and legal restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop an Information Action Plan (Activity 2.1 requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Activity objectives: determine incident information needs; conduct an assessment of Information Team members’ skills, experiences, and training needs; assign PIOs to tasks and determine how many more PIOs will be needed. Groups must identify information needs/priorities, tasks with corresponding personnel assigned, and explain assessment of Information Team members. Hint: address the who, what, where, and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the who/what/where/why framework: 'who' = team member assigned; 'what' = incident needs; 'where' = where needed most; 'why' = based on assessment of team members. Record on an easel chart and present findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and documenting PIO activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor and document PIO activities (header present: MONITORING AND DOCUMENTING OF PIO ACTIVITIES).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep activity logs (e.g., ICS Form 214 Activity Log), message pads, and records of press releases, briefings, and media interactions for accountability and continuity.
